body.statement: Suppose both normalized PPML fits exist uniquely, the panel contains one observation per unit and period, the Moreau--Kastler fit uses equal observation weights with no covariates or offsets, and \(n_g/N=p_g\) for every \(g\in C\). Profiling its individual fixed effects gives the cohort-mean PPML time-score equations and \(\sum_{i=1}^{n_g}\widehat\mu^{\mathrm{MK}}_{git}=n_g\widehat\mu_{gt}\); consequently \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{MK}}^{\mathrm{ind}}=\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{CM}}\).
body.justification: The proposition proves a deterministic point-estimator identity under exact aggregation conditions; that identity is needed for the positive-cycle counterexample but, by itself, transfers no semiparametric efficiency bound.
body.gap: Moreau--Kastler (2025, printed pp. 15 and 20--23, equations (3.1), (3.2), (3.13), (3.14), and (3.19)) presents the individual specification and imputation estimator but not the profiling identity with the cohort-mean rank-one score or any cross-experiment efficiency transfer.
body.consumer: Applied users can test whether their implementation lies on the exact aggregation boundary and can avoid treating point-estimator coincidence as evidence that two statistical experiments share an efficiency bound.
